question: How does the national health insurance thing work for foreign students in Korea?
required_facts: International students must join National Health Insurance (mandatory since March 2021)
NHIS mails the bill to the address on the Alien Registration Card; pay monthly by the deadline (auto-transfer possible)
Monthly premium from March 1, 2026: 79,320 won
Late or missing payment hurts visa/stay extension; up to 5% late fees and limited benefits
reference_answer: National Health Insurance is mandatory for international students in Korea (since March 2021). The NHIS sends a monthly bill to the address on your Alien Registration Card and you pay it by the deadline (auto-transfer is possible); from March 1, 2026 the premium is 79,320 won a month. With NHI you pay only part of the cost (20% inpatient, 30-60% outpatient) and need no claim; unpaid premiums hurt stay-extension reviews and add up to 5% late fees.
notes: National rule; ERICA NHI page and Seoul notices agree. Persona is applicant but the question does not state it (scope default). 2025 premium notice outdated.

ERICA: the 25,000 won premium appears on the tuition bill
reference_answer: Yes. Seoul: Hanyang runs a private insurance separate from NHI; enrolled students are covered by the university budget, and students who completed coursework pay 25,000 won themselves. ERICA: the 25,000 won group-insurance premium is added to your tuition bill.
notes: Campus unstated and the payment route differs; academic_status splits the Seoul answer. Distinct values: university pays vs 25,000 won, so two branches.

question: What documents do I need to prepare before I can do a part-time job?

Copy of Alien Registration Card, employment contract and copy of the employer's Business Registration Certificate
Transcript or Certificate of Enrollment and proof of Korean (or English) proficiency

Prepare the Part-time Work Confirmation Form (signed by the university's person in charge of international students), a copy of your Alien Registration Card, the employment contract, a copy of the employer's Business Registration Certificate, a transcript or certificate of enrollment, and proof of Korean (or English) proficiency, plus the application form and passport. The work may start only after the permit is granted.
notes: Immigration permit, national; Seoul checklist and ERICA visa page list the same documents. Visiting D-2-8 6-month wait (ERICA page) is an eligibility caveat, not about documents.

question: What is alien registration and when do I have to do it?
required_facts: Foreigners staying in Korea more than 90 days must register as aliens (get an Alien Registration/Residence Card)
Register within 90 days of entry; immediately when granted a status or a change of status
Late registration means a fine; group registration via the OIA each semester, or book individually on HiKorea
reference_answer: Alien registration is the immigration registration (giving you an Alien Registration Card) that every foreigner staying in Korea more than 90 days must complete. You must register within 90 days of entering Korea, or immediately when you are granted a residence status or a change of status; missing the deadline means a fine. Check the OIA's group-registration notice each semester, or book an appointment on HiKorea and apply at the immigration office yourself.
notes: National immigration rule; ERICA visa page.

question: What are outgoing programs and what are the benefits?

question: How do I take a break from my studies and come back later?
required_facts: Seoul: leave-of-absence notice posted on the OIA board each semester; one year at a time (max 3 years, undergrad); re-register online in the re-registration period or be dismissed
Seoul re-registration: online only (no in-person/e-mail), passport copy and bank balance certificate (USD 16,000 / KRW 20,000,000)

question: How do I extend my stay? My card expires soon.
required_facts: Apply for extension of stay from 4 months before the card/visa expires, no later than the expiry date

notes: National immigration rule; ERICA visa page gives the procedure. Extra-semester supervisor form (a6beb530) is a caveat.

question: Do I have to file an entry report when I arrive?
